lane: W70-B DeepMind-style comparator (challenge + solution + direct comparator, NO Lean)
title: Erdos #142 (prize $10000): asymptotic formula for r_k(N)
statement_frozen: Let r_k(N) be the largest possible size of a subset of {1,...,N} that does not contain any non-trivial k-term arithmetic progression. Prove an asymptotic formula for r_k(N).
statement_source: frozen corpus statement (BRIEFING.md, campaign 4c4a072); restatements must preserve it EXACTLY

conventions.non_trivial_k_ap: a, a+d, ..., a+(k-1)d with integer a >= 1 and common difference d >= 1 (non-trivial = d >= 1 = terms pairwise distinct)
conventions.r_k_definition: r_k(N) = max { |S| : S is a subset of {1,...,N} and S contains no non-trivial k-term arithmetic progression }
conventions.k_domain: integer k >= 2 (k = 1 is degenerate and excluded; the campaign certifies the k = 2 edge exactly and k = 3,4,5 finite tables)
conventions.universe: integer intervals [1,N] with N a positive integer

r3_exact_table.method_1: iterative-deepening DFS branch-and-bound with pair-ban propagation + exact-suffix bounds + memoization
r3_exact_table.method_2: z3 SAT/UNSAT dual certificates (SAT model re-validated + cardinality-UNSAT upper bound)

r4_exact_table.method_1: generalized k-AP branch-and-bound (AP-mask include-checks + exact-suffix bounds + memoization)

r5_exact_table.method_1: generalized k-AP branch-and-bound (AP-mask include-checks + exact-suffix bounds + memoization)

block_upper_envelope.beyond_exhaustive: randomized greedy-order + dense-sieve + leave-one-residue + Cantor structured constructions, every set re-validated by an independent (a,d)-scan checker

monotonicity_law.statement: r_{k+1}(N) >= r_k(N) for every k >= 2 and N >= 1 (a (k+1)-term AP contains a k-term AP: its first k terms), hence every k-AP-free set is (k+1)-AP-free
monotonicity_law.machine_check: r_2(N) <= r_3(N) <= r_4(N) <= r_5(N) on the certified tables N = 1..20

acceptance_criteria: AC-1 (exact tables with certificates): every claimed exact value r_k(N) must be reproduced by at least two independent comparator methods where the parameter space demands it (r_3: B&B + z3 dual certs N<=16 + brute N<=12; r_4/r_5: B&B + z3 dual certs N<=12), and every exhibited maximum-size witness must be re-validated as a subset of [1,N] that is k-AP-free under the pinned (a,d) convention by an independent checker.

AC-2 (lower bounds as witnesses): every claimed lower bound must come with an explicit witness family spec; the comparator must generate the family itself (two independent generation routes), verify its cardinality, verify containment in the claimed universe, and verify AP-freeness by full pair-midpoint scan plus an independent (a,d)-scan.

AC-3 (upper bounds with proofs-of-validity on the finite envelope): every claimed universal upper bound must hold on the comparator's exhaustive envelope (all k-AP-free maxima for N<=16, k=3..6) and on a torture corpus of randomized/structured k-AP-free constructions for 17<=N<=60, each re-validated independently.
AC-4 (agreement law): every comparator-derived value must EQUAL the solution.json claim exactly; any disagreement is a CRITICAL rejection (exit 2).

AC-5 (negative controls / non-vacuity): the comparator must REJECT a deliberately corrupted table (one entry bumped), must flag a crippled (bound minus one) block bound, and must reject a deliberately AP-containing witness; failure of any negative control to trigger is itself a failure.

AC-6 (honest labels): the solution must label every claim exactly (exact-table / witness-lower-bound / envelope-upper-bound / edge-case / open-scope declaration); the comparator checks the labels are present and that the open-scope declaration is not contradicted (no asymptotic claim is certified).

disambiguation_cap_set_vs_142.note: HONEST DISTINCTION (binding): DeepMind/FunSearch's headline cap-set result lives in the affine space F_3^n (no three distinct collinear vectors); Erdos #142 lives in integer intervals [1,N] (no non-trivial k-term AP). Both are 3-AP-free extremal problems and both admit digit/no-carry constructions, but they are DIFFERENT problems; a cap-set record neither solves nor bounds #142. The comparator machine-checks only the shadow fact that both use ternary-digit ideas: the integer-interval Cantor family T_8 has 2^8-1 = 255 elements inside [1, 3^8-1] (255/6561 ~ 3.9% density) while FunSearch's cap set has 512 elements inside F_3^8 (512/6561 ~ 7.8%) - related constructions, distinct problems, no comparability claim.
disambiguation_cap_set_vs_142.funsearch_cap_set_record: cap set of size 512 in dimension n = 8 over F_3, discovered by FunSearch - per the Nature 2024 paper: 'The function priority: Z_3^n -> R discovered by FunSearch that results in a cap set of size 512 in n = 8 dimensions' and 'we do not just discover the set of 512 eight-dimensional vectors in itself, but a program that generates it'
disambiguation_cap_set_vs_142.label: context baseline (DeepMind public result, fetched 2026-11 from the Nature page URL below); NOT a verification target

deepmind_methodology.funsearch_evaluator_loop: FunSearch (Function Search): 'an evolutionary procedure based on pairing a pretrained LLM with a systematic evaluator' (Nature 2024 abstract); candidate programs are verified DIRECTLY against the evaluator - no proof assistant in the loop.
deepmind_methodology.alphacode_test_based_grading: AlphaCode (Li et al., 'Competition-level code generation with AlphaCode', Science 378, 1092-1097, 2022): candidate solutions graded by running them against test cases (test-based grading), not by proof.
deepmind_methodology.what_this_comparator_is: The DeepMind evaluation methodology applied to Erdos #142: challenge.json = the frozen spec; solution.json = the campaign's claimed results (each honestly labeled); comparator.py = the independent evaluator that DIRECTLY verifies every claim computationally (exact integer arithmetic, z3 + gmpy2 + brute force cross-checks). NO Lean anywhere in this lane.
deepmind_methodology.label: methodology context (canonical citations)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: Behrend lower bound (k=3)
sota_baselines_142_proper.statement: r_3(N) >= N * exp(-C*sqrt(log N)) for an absolute constant C (spheres-in-base construction; lifts to every fixed k >= 3 because a 3-AP-free set is automatically k-AP-free)
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: F. A. Behrend, 'On sets of integers which contain no three terms in arithmetical progression', Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 32 (1946) 331-332
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: context baseline, canonical citation (NOT verified by the comparator)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: Roth theorem (k=3)
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: K. F. Roth, 'On certain sets of integers', J. London Math. Soc. 28 (1953) 104-109
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: context baseline, canonical citation (NOT verified by the comparator)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: Bloom-Sisask upper bound (k=3)
sota_baselines_142_proper.statement: r_3(N) <= N / (log N)^(1+c) for an absolute constant c > 0
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: T. F. Bloom, O. Sisask, 'Breaking the logarithmic barrier in Roth's theorem on arithmetic progressions', arXiv:2007.03528 (2020)
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: context baseline, canonical citation (NOT verified by the comparator)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: Kelley-Meka upper bound (k=3, current best shape)
sota_baselines_142_proper.statement: r_3(N) <= N * exp(-c*(log N)^(1/12)) for an absolute constant c > 0
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: Z. Kelley, R. Meka, 'Strong bounds for 3-progressions', Proc. 55th ACM STOC (2023); simplification by Bloom-Sisask 2023
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: context baseline, canonical citation (NOT verified by the comparator)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: Green-Tao upper bound (k=4)
sota_baselines_142_proper.statement: r_4(N) <= N / (log N)^c for some constant c > 0
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: B. Green, T. Tao, 'New bounds for Szemerédi's theorem, II: a new bound for r_4(N)', Ann. Math. 185 (2017) 339-415
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: context baseline, canonical citation (NOT verified by the comparator)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: k >= 5 upper bounds (logarithmic-strength savings only)
sota_baselines_142_proper.statement: for fixed k >= 5 the best known upper bounds save only a logarithmic-type factor over N (Gowers 2001 quantitative hypergraph-removal shape N/(log log N)^{c_k}, with recent improvements by Leng-Sah-Sawhney); no N^(1-eps) upper bound is known for any fixed k >= 4, and no asymptotic formula is known for ANY k >= 3
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: W. T. Gowers, 'A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem', Geom. Funct. Anal. 11 (2001) 465-588; J. Leng, A. Sah, M. Sawhney, 'Improved bounds for Szemerédi's theorem', 2024
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: context baseline, canonical citation (NOT verified by the comparator)

sota_baselines_142_proper.name: monotonicity shadow (machine-checked)
sota_baselines_142_proper.statement: r_{k+1}(N) >= r_k(N) for k >= 2 (a (k+1)-AP contains a k-AP as its first k terms); hence Behrend-type lower bounds lift to every fixed k >= 3 and no fixed-k r_k(N) is O(log N)
sota_baselines_142_proper.citation: elementary; machine-checked by the comparator on the certified tables
sota_baselines_142_proper.label: machine-checked shadow of the context (the ONLY context item the comparator certifies)
